Normalization of an algebraic curve

 Home Mathematics Area of mathematics Geometry and topology Algebraic geometry
OurBigBook.com Words: 11k Articles: 199
This is the one-dimensional case of normalization of an algebraic variety, constructed from integral closures of coordinate rings.
The normalization of an irreducible algebraic curve is a normal, hence regular, curve with a finite birational morphism to the original curve. Over a perfect field this regular curve is smooth.

Finite normalization model of a one-variable function field (K/k,trdegk​K=1)

Words: 68
Normalization of an algebraic curve OurBigBook.com
For an algebraically closed field k and a finitely generated field extension K/k of transcendence degree one, choose t with K/k(t) finite. The integral closures of the two standard coordinate rings of the projective line in K are finite modules and glue to a finite normalization of an algebraic curve of the projective line. A one-dimensional normal local ring is a discrete valuation ring; over the perfect field k the resulting projective curve is smooth. Extension of rational maps gives uniqueness of this smooth projective model.

Flat normalization is an isomorphism

Words: 71
Normalization of an algebraic curve OurBigBook.com
If the normalization of an integral scheme is flat, then it is an isomorphism. On an affine chart, let A⊆B⊆Frac(A) be the integral closure. Integrality gives surjectivity on spectra, so flatness makes B faithfully flat. For b=u/v∈B with u,v∈A and v=0, faithful flatness gives vB∩A=vA. Thus u=va for some a∈A, and b=a. Consequently B=A. This proof does not need finiteness of the normalization.

Geometric genus (g(C))

Normalization of an algebraic curve OurBigBook.com
The geometric genus of an irreducible curve is the genus of its smooth projective normalization.

Genus one curve

Words: 11k Articles: 193
Geometric genus OurBigBook.com
A genus one curve is a smooth projective curve of geometric genus one. Choosing a rational point makes it an elliptic curve.

Elliptic curve

Words: 11k Articles: 192
Genus one curve OurBigBook.com
An elliptic curve over a field K is a smooth projective curve of genus one equipped with a specified K-rational point O. The chord-and-tangent law makes its rational points an abelian group with identity O.
Galois cohomology of an elliptic curve (Hi(K,E))
Words: 73
Elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
For an elliptic curve E/K, regard E(Ksep) as a discrete Galois module for the absolute Galois group GK​. Its continuous Galois cohomology has H0(K,E)=E(K); H1(K,E) classifies torsors under E. For an integer n invertible in K, the Kummer exact sequence of an elliptic curve gives 0→E(K)/nE(K)→H1(K,E[n])→H1(K,E)[n]→0. If [n]Q=P, the first map sends P to σ↦σQ−Q. Changing Q changes the cocycle by a coboundary; this class vanishes exactly when P has a division point over K.
Diagonal cubic elliptic curve (X3+Y3+dZ3=0)
Words: 478 Articles: 3
Elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
For d∈Q×, the smooth projective curve X3+Y3+dZ3=0, with identity O=(1:−1:0), is a genus-one elliptic curve. Its partial derivatives have no common projective zero. The invertible linear projective transformation
(X:Y:Z)=(−12dZ:−36d(X−Y):X+Y)
(1)
sends it to Y2Z=X3−432d2Z3, taking O to (0:1:0). Indeed (X+Y)3+3(X+Y)(X−Y)2=4(X3+Y3)=−4dZ3. In affine coordinates u=X/Z,v=Y/Z, this gives x=−12d/(u+v) and y=−36d(u−v)/(u+v), with inverse u=(y−36d)/(6x), v=(−y−36d)/(6x). Thus diagonal sums of two cubes are naturally studied through elliptic-curve addition formula.
Rational pairs of cubes summing to seven (u3+v3=7)
Words: 104
Diagonal cubic elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
There are infinitely many rational pairs (u,v) with u3+v3=7. The corresponding Weierstrass equation of an elliptic curve is y2=x3−21168, and (u,v)=(2,−1) maps to P=(84,756). The primes 5 and 11 are good, with point counts 6 and 12 because cubing is bijective in their residue fields. Reduction of torsion points on an elliptic curve bounds rational torsion by order dividing 6. The flexes of a diagonal cubic exclude three-torsion for d=−7, while d/2=−7/2 is not a cube and hence excludes two-torsion. Thus P has infinite order.
All nonzero multiples of P map to distinct rational affine pairs, since the only rational point at infinity of the diagonal cubic is its identity. The inverse map is u=(y+252)/(6x) and v=(252−y)/(6x).
Rational torsion of a diagonal cubic (Ed​(Q)tors​)
Words: 185
Diagonal cubic elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
For d∈Q× the rational torsion subgroup of X3+Y3+dZ3=0 is cyclic of order 3 if d is a cube, cyclic of order 2 if d/2 is a cube, and trivial otherwise.
To bound torsion, use the Weierstrass equation of an elliptic curve y2=x3−432d2. At every good prime ℓ≡2(mod3), cubing is a bijection on Fℓ​, so the number of points is ℓ+1. Reduction injects the prime-to-ℓ torsion, since multiplication by an integer prime to ℓ is invertible in the formal group of an elliptic curve. For any prime q>3, the Dirichlet theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions supplies a good ℓ≡2(mod3), ℓ≡1(modq), excluding q-torsion. Good primes ℓ≡5(mod12) exclude order 4, and good primes ℓ≡11(mod18) exclude order 9. Thus every rational torsion point is killed by 6.
The flexes of a diagonal cubic give rational three-torsion exactly when d is a cube, and then it has order 3. Rational two-torsion requires x3=432d2, whose sole possible rational root exists exactly when d/2 is a cube. This equivalence follows by comparing prime valuations modulo 3, including the valuation at 2. The two conditions cannot hold together because 2 is not a rational cube. The asserted classification follows.
Flexes of a diagonal cubic (Ed​[3])
Words: 114
Diagonal cubic elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
Let r3=d=0 and let ζ be a primitive cube root of unity. The nine inflection points of a plane cubic on X3+Y3+dZ3=0 are
(1:−ζj:0),(0:−rζj:1),(−rζj:0:1),j=0,1,2.
(2)
The Hessian criterion for flexes of a plane cubic gives the Hessian determinant 216dXYZ, so every flex lies on one of the three coordinate lines. Their intersections give precisely the displayed points. With (1:−1:0) as identity, these are exactly the three-torsion points are flexes of a plane cubic configurations: the tangent divisor at a flex is 3P, giving 3(P−O)=0.
Over Q only the first point with j=0 is rational on Z=0. The other two coordinate lines each give one rational point precisely when d is a rational cube. Consequently the rational three-torsion subgroup is Z/3Z when d is a cube and is trivial otherwise.
Elliptic curve group law from Riemann-Roch (E(k)≅Pic0(E))
Words: 62
Elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
Fix O∈E(k). On a genus-one smooth projective curve, every degree-one divisor class has a unique effective point representative by the Riemann-Roch theorem: its section space has dimension one, since the complementary canonical-divisor degree is negative. Thus P↦[P−O] is a bijection onto the degree-zero Picard group of a curve. Transporting divisor-class addition proves the group axioms, with identity O, and characterizes P+Q by P+Q∼R+O.
Three-torsion points are flexes of a plane cubic (3(P−O)=0)
Words: 108
Elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
Let E be a smooth plane cubic with an inflection point O as identity. A point P with 3(P−O)=0 in Picard group has a line whose intersection divisor with E is 3P. Indeed, OE​(3P)≅OE​(3O)≅OE​(1). On this genus-one curve, the Riemann-Roch theorem gives h0(OE​(1))=3: the dual term has negative degree. Restriction of ambient linear forms is injective and its source also has dimension three, so it is an isomorphism. The section vanishing at 3P therefore comes from a line. Conversely, such a line gives 3P∼3O, so P is a three-torsion point. This includes O; points of exact order three are the other such points.
Complex uniformization of an elliptic curve (E(C)≃C/L)
Words: 55
Elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
Every complex elliptic curve, as a complex Lie group, is the quotient of C by a rank-two lattice. The coordinate functions are built from the Weierstrass elliptic function and its derivative. Holomorphic group homomorphisms lift to scalar multiplication on C, and their endomorphism condition is aL⊆L. This turns complex multiplication into a statement about lattice stabilizers.
Weierstrass uniformization by half-period values (C/Λ≅{y2=4x3−g2​x−g3​}∪{O})
Words: 117
Elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
The Weierstrass elliptic function and its derivative give an isomorphism z↦(℘(z),℘′(z)) from a one-dimensional complex torus to a smooth plane cubic, with 0 sent to its identity at infinity. The three nonzero two-torsion points of a complex torus are zeros of ℘′. Its triple pole implies that these three zeros are simple. If two half-period values of the Weierstrass elliptic function coincided, ℘−e would have at least four zeros counted with multiplicity, contradicting its double pole. The three cubic roots are therefore distinct, proving smoothness of an algebraic variety. The degree-two map ℘ has fibers {z,−z}, distinguished by ℘′ away from the half-periods, proving bijectivity. A line pulls back to an elliptic function with a triple pole, and the zero-pole sum of an elliptic function says that its three intersections sum to zero on the torus. This gives exactly the chord-and-tangent group law, including repeated intersections interpreted by intersection multiplicity.
Nonparametrizability of an elliptic curve
Words: 47
Elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
An elliptic curve in characteristic zero admits no nonconstant rational map of projective varieties from the projective line. Over C, write its equation as y2=∏j=13​(x−ej​) with distinct ej​. Substituting x=u/v with coprime polynomials gives (yv2)2=v∏j​(u−ej​v). These four pairwise coprime factors must all be squares. The polynomial pencil with four square members forces u,v constant, ruling out a nonconstant rational parametrization of an algebraic curve.
j-invariant of an elliptic curve (j(E)=c43​/Δ)
Words: 59
Elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
The j-invariant is unchanged by admissible changes of Weierstrass equation of an elliptic curve. With b2​=a12​+4a2​ and b4​=a1​a3​+2a4​, set c4​=b22​−24b4​ and j=c43​/Δ, where Δ is the elliptic-curve discriminant. For good reduction over a local field, an integral equation with unit discriminant shows that j lies in the valuation ring. Thus a negative valuation of j proves bad reduction, even if the displayed equation has not been proved minimal.
Abel-Jacobi map of a genus-one curve (P↦[P−O])
Words: 148 Articles: 1
Elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
Let E be a genus one curve over an algebraically closed field and choose O∈E. The map
E⟶Cl0(E),P⟼[P−O]
(3)
is an isomorphism. For a degree-zero divisor D, Riemann--Roch gives a nonzero section of D+O, so D∼P−O for some point P. If P−O∼P′−O with P=P′, a rational function with divisor P−P′ would give a degree-one map to the projective line, contradicting that E has genus one. The Abel--Jacobi map transports addition in the divisor class group to the elliptic-curve group law.
Involution of a degree-two map from a genus one curve (ι(p)=s−p)
Words: 62
Abel-Jacobi map of a genus-one curve OurBigBook.com
Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two, a degree-two map from a smooth genus one curve to the projective line has a deck involution. After choosing an origin, all its fiber divisors on an algebraic curve are linearly equivalent and have the same group sum s, by the Abel-Jacobi map of a genus-one curve. The involution is consequently p↦s−p, including its fixed ramification points. Composing two such involutions gives a translation on an elliptic curve.
Chord-and-tangent group law
Words: 387 Articles: 6
Elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
On a smooth plane cubic with identity point O, a line through points P and Q, interpreted as the tangent when P=Q, meets the cubic in a third point R. The chord-and-tangent group law defines P+Q as the third intersection of the line through R and O with the cubic.
Torsion multiples in a two-parameter Weierstrass family (y2+axy+by=x3+bx2,P=(0,0))
Words: 67
Chord-and-tangent group law OurBigBook.com
Assume the elliptic-curve discriminant is nonzero. Then b=0, and tangency at P gives 2P=(−b,b(a−1)) and −2P=(−b,0). The line through P,2P has slope 1−a and gives 3P=(1−a,a−b−1), −3P=(1−a,(1−a)2). Consequently P has exact order four when a=1, exact order five when a=b+1, and exact order six when b=(a−1)(2−a). The nonsingularity condition excludes the zero values of b that would otherwise invalidate these torsion conclusions.
Associativity of the chord-and-tangent law via divisor classes
Words: 84
Chord-and-tangent group law OurBigBook.com
For a smooth genus one curve with origin O, the map P↦[(P)−(O)] identifies geometric points with the degree-zero Picard group of a curve. Riemann-Roch theorem gives a unique effective representative for each divisor class of degree one: its Riemann-Roch space has dimension one. A line cuts a plane cubic in a divisor linearly equivalent to 3(O) when O is the Weierstrass flex. The two successive line intersections in the chord-and-tangent group law therefore give addition of the corresponding divisor classes. Associativity follows by injectivity of the identification and associativity of divisor-class addition, including tangent intersection multiplicities.

Bad reduction of an elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
Discriminants of isomorphic Weierstrass equations of an elliptic curve differ by a twelfth power of the scale parameter, so their valuations differ by a multiple of twelve. An integral model with good reduction has discriminant valuation zero. Thus a displayed integral model with discriminant valuation not divisible by twelve proves intrinsic bad reduction. More generally, a displayed discriminant valuation between zero and eleven is already minimal, since any smaller integral-model valuation would be nonnegative and differ by twelve. Positive valuations divisible by twelve alone do not establish bad reduction; rescaling may remove them.

Isogeny of elliptic curves OurBigBook.com
The group HomK​(E1​,E2​) consists of morphisms of elliptic curves defined over K that preserve the group operation, with pointwise addition. Its zero element is the constant map to the identity. Every nonzero element is an isogeny of elliptic curves: its image is a closed connected subgroup of the target, so nonconstancy makes it the whole curve, and a nonconstant morphism of smooth projective curves is finite. The degree of an isogeny extends to this group by assigning degree zero to the zero homomorphism.

Pull it back along (ϕ,ψ) and take degrees. This gives the degree parallelogram law, even when one homomorphism equals plus or minus the other: bundle restriction remains valid in these cases.
It implies q(nϕ)=n2q(ϕ) by the second-difference recursion, and polarization gives the symmetric bilinear form B(ϕ,ψ)=(q(ϕ+ψ)−q(ϕ−ψ))/4. To check additivity, the parallelogram law gives B(x+z,y)+B(x−z,y)=2B(x,y); interchange x,z and use oddness to get B(x+z,y)−B(x−z,y)=2B(z,y). Adding proves bilinearity. Since a nonzero isogeny has positive degree, q is positive on every nonzero element. On every finite-dimensional rational span the matrix of B is rational. Positivity on rational vectors implies nonnegativity on real vectors by density; a nontrivial kernel of a rational matrix would contain a nonzero rational vector. Hence the real extension is positive definite. This proves the positive-definite quadratic form property, rather than only a parallelogram identity.

For positive integral k, the rational torsion subgroup of y2=x3+kx has order dividing four. Indeed, torsion-freeness of the formal group over Qp for odd p, reduction of torsion points on an elliptic curve, and the point-count criterion for y squared equals x cubed plus k x bound its order by p+1 at all good primes p≡3(mod4). The canonical height pairing is ⟨P,Q⟩=(h(P+Q)−h(P)−h(Q))/2. The height parallelogram identity makes it bilinear. It descends through torsion and is positive definite on the free part of the Mordell-Weil group. The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives h(P−Q)≤2h(P)+2h(Q), useful for height descent.
Rank certificate from rounded canonical heights
Words: 93
Canonical height pairing OurBigBook.com
The Gram matrix of the canonical height pairing of rational points gives a robust independence certificate. For two points, set a=h(P), b=h(Q) and c=(h(P+Q)−a−b)/2. If bounds from rounded measurements imply a>0 and ab−c2>0, the matrix is positive-definite. Any integer relation rP+sQ=O would give ar2+2crs+bs2=0, forcing r=s=0. Thus the points generate a free abelian group of rank two. Checking an interval lower bound for the determinant, rather than just its approximate central value, makes the certificate insensitive to rounding. It certifies independence, not that the points are a basis of the entire Mordell-Weil group.

Mordell-Weil group OurBigBook.com
The saturation of a subgroup H of the Mordell-Weil group consists of all points with a positive multiple in H. Saturation includes the full torsion subgroup. For a full-rank H containing that torsion, it equals E(K), but the index of H may exceed one. Checking that ℓP∈H forces P∈H for every prime divisor of a certified index bound proves that H is already the whole group. A canonical height pairing proves independence of found points; saturation answers the separate question of whether a full-rank subgroup is the full group.

Unramified division torsors at good primes (v∤m,E good at v)
Words: 167
Kummer exact sequence of an elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
At a prime of good reduction of an elliptic curve with residue characteristic not dividing m, multiplication by m extends to a finite étale map of the smooth proper elliptic group scheme over the valuation ring. A local rational point extends to a section by properness. Its division fibre is therefore a finite étale torsor, so the Kummer map of an elliptic curve gives an unramified cohomology class. This bounds ramification in the Weak Mordell-Weil theorem.
A direct proof describes the coordinates, not only the cohomology class. Reduce P by properness and choose a point Q​ with [m]Q​=P over a finite extension of the residue field. Over the corresponding unramified extension of the complete local field, lift Q​ by the Hensel lemma. The error [m]Q0​−P is in the kernel of reduction of an elliptic curve; prime-to-residue-characteristic multiplication on a formal group corrects it uniquely. There is no m-torsion in that kernel, even after a ramified field extension, so every division point with that reduction equals this unramified lift. Consequently all division points of an elliptic curve above P have unramified coordinate fields. The torsion case is discussed in J. S. Milne's Elliptic Curves, Chapter V, Proposition 8.1.

Coverings surviving all local solubility tests need not have rational points. The quotient of an isogeny Selmer group by the rational-point image is a kernel in the Tate–Shafarevich group. Halving cocycle with rational two-torsion OurBigBook.com
Let E:y2=(x−α)(x−β)(x−γ) with distinct algebraic integers in a number field K. For a rational point P, its halving field is unramified outside the finite set S of primes dividing 2(α−β)(α−γ)(β−γ). At v∈/S, the elliptic-curve discriminant is a unit, so there is good reduction. A half of the reduction of P is defined over a finite extension of the residue field. Pass to the corresponding unramified extension of the completion and lift this half using the Hensel lemma. The doubling error lies in the formal kernel of a minimal Weierstrass equation. Since two is a unit, prime-to-residue-characteristic multiplication on a formal group corrects this error uniquely. Every half differs by rational 2-torsion, so all halves are unramified at v. The halving cocycle with rational two-torsion has image of order at most four, making the halving field a Galois extension of degree at most four. The bounded-degree extensions with restricted ramification are finite in number; there are only finitely many homomorphisms from their finite Galois groups to E[2]. Thus E(K)/2E(K) is finite, without assuming any form of the Mordell-Weil theorem.

Suppose the ring of integers of a number field is a principal ideal domain, a,b are integral, and b is a unit. On y2=x(x2+ax+b) every nonzero x-coordinate has even valuation at every finite prime: positive valuation gives 2v(y)=v(x), and negative valuation gives 2v(y)=3v(x). This can reduce a two-isogeny descent to a very small calculation even though the field contains no ordering.

Five-adic obstruction to square class two on the curve with coefficient one hundred (W2=2U4+50V4)

Quartic covering in a two-isogeny descent OurBigBook.com
This quartic has no primitive integral solution. If 5∤U, reduction modulo five makes W2≡2, impossible. If 5∣U, coprimality gives 5∤V and 5∣W; dividing by twenty-five then gives (W/5)2≡2V4≡2(mod5), again impossible. It excludes the square class two in two-isogeny descent on Y2=X3+100X. The point (5,25) supplies class five, so the subgroup property excludes class ten as well.
Signed divisor-two obstruction for an isogeny covering (W2=±2U4+24U2V2±32V4)

Quartic covering in a two-isogeny descent OurBigBook.com
The two-isogeny descent quartics associated with square classes 2 and −2 on Y2=X3+24X2+64X have no rational points. A rational solution can be scaled to integral W,U,V with coprime integers U,V. If U is odd, reduction modulo sixteen gives 2 or 10 for the positive class, and 14 or 6 for the negative class; none is a quadratic residue. If U=2u is even, then V is odd and the right side is 32(±u4+3u2V2±V4), with the same sign on the two signed terms. The bracket is odd, so its 2-adic valuation is exactly five, impossible for a nonzero square. These two parity cases exhaust primitive solutions.
Modulo-thirty-two obstruction for a congruent-number descent class (N2=2(U4+p2V4))

Quartic covering in a two-isogeny descent OurBigBook.com
If p≡3(mod8), this quartic covering in a two-isogeny descent has no primitive integral solution. Opposite parities of U,V give N2≡2(mod8). If both are odd, their fourth powers are one modulo sixteen and p2≡9(mod16), giving N2≡20(mod32). Neither residue is a square. This excludes the class 2 on Y2=X3+4p2X.
Odd-prime obstructions for the congruent-number isogeny coverings (p≡3(mod4))

Quartic covering in a two-isogeny descent OurBigBook.com
For the curve Y2=X3+4p2X with p≡3(mod4), the classes p and 2p in two-isogeny descent lead to N2=p(U4+4V4) and N2=2p(U4+V4). A primitive solution forces p∣N and p∤V. The resulting congruences make −1 a square modulo p, a contradiction. Thus these coverings have no rational points.

A proposed square class in a two-isogeny descent can be excluded by testing its quartic modulo 8. For N2=3U4+5U2V2−2V4 with gcd(U,V)=1, both variables odd give residue 6; odd-even gives 3 or 7; even-odd gives 6 or 2. None is a square modulo 8, excluding class 3 and, by the subgroup property of the descent image, its entire coset.

Rank bound for a prime congruent-number elliptic curve (rankEp​(Q)≤2)
Words: 66
Congruent number elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
For an odd prime p, let Ep​:y2=x3−p2x. Its two-isogeny descent partner is Ep′​:y2=x3+4p2x. The first two-torsion square-class homomorphism has image exactly {1,−1,p,−p}: prime-support bounds allow only these classes, and the four rational two-torsion points realize all of them. Every nonidentity point on Ep′​ has positive x, so its square-class image is contained in {1,2,p,2p}. The two-isogeny rank formula gives 2rankEp​=#α′(Ep′​)≤4, hence the rank is at most 2.
Rational torsion of a congruent number curve (ED​(Q)tors​≅(Z/2Z)2)
Words: 59
Congruent number elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
For nonzero integral D, the elliptic curve ED​:y2=x3−D2x has rational torsion precisely O,(0,0),(D,0),(−D,0). At every good prime p≡3(mod4), cancellation of the Legendre symbols at x and −x gives #ED​(Fp​)=p+1. The torsion-freeness of the formal group over Qp for odd p makes the rational torsion subgroup inject into this group. The Dirichlet theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions excludes odd factors of its order and bounds its two-primary part by four. The four displayed rational 2-torsion points then give equality.
Congruent number
Words: 332 Articles: 4
Congruent number elliptic curve OurBigBook.com
A positive integer is a congruent number when it is the area of a right triangle with rational side lengths. For square-free D, this is equivalent to the congruent number elliptic curve having a Mordell-Weil group of positive rank.
Two is not a congruent number (2 is not a congruent number)
Words: 59
Congruent number OurBigBook.com
A primitive Pythagorean triple of area twice a square would satisfy mn(m−n)(m+n)=2s2. Pairwise coprimality makes the odd factors squares and the even factor twice a square. The possibility m even is excluded modulo eight. Thus m=a2,n=2b2,m+n=c2,m−n=d2. The coprime integers u=(c+d)/2,v=(c−d)/2 have uv=b2, hence are themselves squares, and a2=u2+v2 contradicts fourth-power sum cannot be a square. Clearing denominators gives the assertion for rational triangles.
Fermat right triangle theorem
Words: 71
Congruent number OurBigBook.com
There is no positive integer right triangle whose area is a square. For a hypothetical primitive triangle of minimal hypotenuse, its primitive Pythagorean parametrization makes m,n,m−n,m+n pairwise coprime squares. Write m=r2, n=s2, m+n=u2, m−n=v2. Modulo eight forces m odd and n even. The new integer legs (u+v)/2,(u−v)/2 have hypotenuse r and area (s/2)2, a smaller positive hypotenuse, contradicting infinite descent. Clearing denominators extends the conclusion to rational right triangles of area one.
Infinitely many rational right triangles from a nontorsion point
Words: 56
Congruent number OurBigBook.com
For D>0, a nontorsion rational point on the congruent number elliptic curve y2=x3−D2x gives infinitely many positive rational right triangles of area D. Apply the formulas a=∣(x2−D2)/y∣, b=∣2Dx/y∣, c=∣(x2+D2)/y∣ to its multiples. The map is finite-to-one: if r=c/b is fixed, then ∣x∣ satisfies X2−2DrX+D2=0, leaving only finitely many coordinate signs. Thus infinitely many points give infinitely many distinct triangles.
Noncongruent primes congruent to three modulo eight (p≡3(mod8)⟹p is not congruent)
Words: 112
Congruent number OurBigBook.com
For a prime p≡3(mod8), apply two-isogeny descent to the congruent number elliptic curve y2=x3−p2x and its companion y2=x3+4p2x. The first square-class image is exactly {1,−1,p,−p}, already supplied by 2-torsion. The second has only positive candidates 1,2,p,2p. The quartic covering in a two-isogeny descent equations for p and 2p are impossible modulo p, because −1 is not a quadratic residue. For 2 the equation is W2=2U4+2p2V4. Coprimality forces U,V odd and W=2Z; modulo sixteen this gives 2Z2=1+9=10, which is impossible. Thus the second image is trivial and the square-class index formula for two-isogeny descent gives rank zero. The same prime-reduction argument bounds its rational torsion by four, and it already has four rational 2-torsion points, so it has no rational point corresponding to a right triangle of area p.

Euler theorem on four squares in arithmetic progression
Words: 31
Mordell-Weil group of y squared equals x times x plus one times x plus four OurBigBook.com
There is no nonconstant four-term arithmetic progression of rational square numbers. If r2,s2,1,t2 formed one, then (−2s2,2rst) would lie on y2=x(x+1)(x+4); its explicitly known Mordell-Weil group forces s2=1 and the common difference to vanish.

This applies normalization of an algebraic curve to the two local branches of a node.
Normalization separates a node's two branches; a rational nodal cubic has normalization P1 and two points above its node.
